title: Home ISP reliably carries interactive AI agent streams
description:
Fresh-session handover. The psyche reports: “there seems to be a problem with my ISP in the house ... Everything works like YouTube, full HD videos, but my AI agents cannot function. They can barely get one letter through this pipe ... when I turn on a VPN, it works.” Later clarification: “my host isnt using the home router, so you wont find anything, this connection works.” The required failing-path vantage is Prometheus, not the current Ouranos connection. Current symptom: “youtube videos can stream, but using codex or claude is almost impossible. sometimes an agent can respond. most times not.” The router has been restarted countless times without success. A temporary Madrid NordVPN tunnel on the working Ouranos path passed fresh web tests but did not address the home-path problem; the psyche turned it off. Diagnose why buffered bulk video remains usable while long-lived interactive Codex/Claude traffic stalls or only occasionally responds.

Subagent IDs for resumption/evidence: /root/hotwire_madrid_vpn (Luna xhigh; interrupted by request while redirecting to read-only Prometheus diagnostics); /root/implement_nordvpn_repair (Ohm, Terra xhigh; interrupted by request during authorized hot OS/Lojix work); /root/analyze_lojix_alignment (Godel, Luna xhigh; completed Lojix alignment analysis); /root/psyche_network_acquisition (Franklin, Luna xhigh; completed psyche acquisition); /root/network_path_diagnostics (completed initial Ouranos path audit); /root/nordvpn_config_audit (completed declarative VPN audit); /root/audit_update_invariants (completed update-drift audit). Do not assume interrupted agents completed any in-flight mutation; inspect live state before resuming.

Adjacent unfinished state, not the network diagnosis: NordVPN repair commit 72bdf77e and CriomOS-home pin commit 1ec9a878 were reported pushed and remotely checked. The psyche authorized a no-reboot hot activation, a fresh Lojix v4 database, and discarding the old database. /root/implement_nordvpn_repair was interrupted before returning terminal activation evidence. Related workspace bead: primary-mjl.6 (Lojix terminal deployment truth).

## Required Skills
management,psyche-interraction,psyche-acquisition,engine-analysis
design: Begin read-only from Prometheus. First prove that its egress traverses the affected home router/ISP; if it does not, identify a valid witness before drawing conclusions. Compare fresh and long-lived Codex/Claude-style streams with YouTube/general bulk transfers on the same path. Measure packet loss, retransmission and reordering, path MTU/PMTUD across packet sizes, MSS, IPv4 versus IPv6, DNS, TLS handshakes, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3/QUIC, streaming cadence, NAT/firewall/offload state, and route asymmetry. Use controls from a known-good path where available. Distinguish application/socket persistence from host, router, and upstream ISP behavior. Mark claims as proven, inferred, or unknown. Do not restart or mutate Prometheus, the router, DNS, firewall, VPN, routes, or services during diagnosis. Produce a concise report with a ranked fault tree and the smallest discriminating intervention. Preserve the separate Lojix/VPN repair state; do not conflate a successful tunnel on the working path with evidence about the home path.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Prometheus is proven to use the affected home-router/ISP path, or the missing vantage is explicitly identified. 2. The Codex/Claude failure is reproduced with timestamps and transport evidence, or a defensible causal boundary explains why it cannot be reproduced. 3. Same-path controls show why buffered video succeeds while interactive AI traffic fails. 4. MTU/PMTUD, loss/reordering, DNS, IP-family, TLS, HTTP/2/3, long-lived sockets, and upstream filtering are each ruled in, ruled out, or left with one precise missing witness. 5. The report identifies a ranked likely cause and a minimal safe fix/test without disrupting Prometheus or remote builds. 6. Any later mutation requires separate explicit approval and has rollback evidence. 7. The interrupted subagent IDs and adjacent Lojix/VPN state are preserved for exact resumption.
notes:
Public-shareable diagnosis written to reports/primary-19c-incident-diagnosis-2026-08-10.md. Read-only evidence rules in intermittent loss/retransmission on the affected Avatel path after the clean local edge, but does not distinguish home-router WAN/NAT/offload from Avatel access/CGNAT/core. Exact missing witness: simultaneous failing-client and router-WAN capture during one authenticated Codex/Claude stall; no network mutation was performed. Bead remains open because the underlying fault is not fixed.
Psyche reports that the ISP identified a faulty main line and is repairing it. This confirms the fault is external to the local host/router configuration and resolves the diagnostic ownership boundary. Post-repair service restoration has not yet been independently verified; reopen if symptoms persist.
close_reason: ISP identified a faulty main line and took ownership of repair. Local diagnosis and public report are complete; no local mutation remains. Restoration is not yet independently verified and the bead may be reopened if symptoms persist.

title: Lojix reports terminal deployment truth across daemon and client upgrades
description: During corrected Codex/Claude deployment 5 on 2026-08-06, Lojix actually reached terminal DeployRejected/ActivationFailed at 23:56:18 and changed the Home Manager profile, but the public phase projection remained Building marker71 then Copying marker73/current marker77. There was no active child. The active daemon was Lojix 0.11.0 while the newly exposed client was 0.17.2; the ordinary client failed with unknown Input short header/EOF, and only an old compatible client could query the stale projection. The daemon journal carried the missing terminal truth. This made a finished failed deployment appear indefinitely in progress.
design: Make daemon/client protocol compatibility explicit and fail with a typed version error before misleading queries. Durable deployment terminal outcome must be independently queryable by deployment identity and must update every current-phase projection atomically with the terminal record. Client upgrades must not outrun the active daemon without an upgrade/compatibility plan. Recovery must reconcile partial activation and source revision; never mutate markers or infer success from profile movement.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Compatible and incompatible client/daemon pairs are version-negotiated and tested. 2. Every terminal success or rejection is durably queryable by deployment ID and reflected in current-phase/list views. 3. A regression witness reproduces ActivationFailed after profile movement and proves queries return terminal failure rather than stale Copying. 4. Lojix upgrade deploys daemon and client in an ordered compatible way. 5. Lost child, lost event, locked store, and partial activation have checkable recovery states. 6. Production daemon/client versions and deployment 5 terminal outcome are reconciled without rewriting history.

title: Data on the intermittently offline USB storage is preserved
description: Read-only audit on 2026-08-06 found /dev/sda is a 29.8GiB Generic USB3 card reader mounted at /run/media/li/storage as ext4. It is idle now and not responsible for current host I/O pressure. Historical kernel evidence is high risk: repeated detach and capacity-zero cycles; on 2026-08-03 the device went offline during a write, ext4 requested shutdown, the journal aborted, and buffer/JBD2 journal-superblock I/O errors were logged. The current mount completed recovery and has no new session errors. Only Nautilus held a read directory descriptor.
design: Preserve data before repair. First inventory and copy irreplaceable contents through a bounded, witnessed read path to known-good storage, without assuming the device remains stable. Then, with explicit disruptive approval, perform controlled unmount and read-only/root health inspection; fsck, reseat, replacement, or writes are separate authorized steps. Do not confuse this historical device fault with current NVMe/Codex I/O pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Important files are identified and backed up to verified healthy storage with checksums or equivalent witnesses. 2. Kernel detach/offline/journal evidence is preserved. 3. No repair or destructive filesystem action occurs before backup and explicit approval. 4. Controlled health assessment determines whether card, reader, cable/port, or filesystem is unsafe, or records the remaining causal boundary. 5. Replacement or repair is verified before trusting the device with writable data.

title: One authoritative user generation survives activation and reboot
description: CriomOS embeds Home Manager while Lojix and manual workflows can activate the standalone Home Manager profile. Historical evidence shows a standalone generation changed live files and units, then reboot or embedded activation reasserted an older system-pinned generation. This dual ownership produces recurrent apparent rollbacks. A separate immediate shadowing bug exposed both the legacy home profile and XDG state profile; CriomOS commit 0a7b20d1 narrows the exported profile set but is not live until a system deployment.
design: Choose and enforce one authoritative owner for user generation, profile symlink, activation, reboot convergence, and rollback. Trace a real Lojix UserEnvironment deployment end to end and record selector, immutable source revision, closure, profile target, activation effects, resolved tools, user units, and post-reboot state. Distinguish file-only realization from live graphical/session mutation. Avoid overlays and second evaluations.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Exactly one component owns the live user generation and profile pointer. 2. Standalone, embedded, Lojix, login, and reboot paths converge to the same declared closure or refuse with a typed conflict. 3. Codex and Claude version resolution is witnessed before activation, after activation, in a new login shell, and after reboot. 4. Actual systemd user-unit reload/start effects are known before approval. 5. Lojix records terminal activation outcome and immutable provenance. 6. Profile-shadowing fix is deployed safely and regression-tested.
notes: 2026-08-06 package update/deploy evidence. Pushed CriomOS-home 9ed195f4c4082ef440f0cf02a411031a9144d492 pinning Codex 0.146.1 and Claude Code 2.1.223 with focused launcher check; pushed CriomOS 74e61a274e5f552fa974a4ccb864522b203d0be3 pinning that Home revision. Official npm and GitHub latest metadata agreed; configured Prometheus remote-builder check passed. After profile cleanup/GC, exactly one Lojix UserEnvironment ActivateNow request was submitted as deployment 5. It reached terminal DeployRejected / ActivationFailed, marker 70: Home Manager partially switched the profile, then activate exited 1 on VS Code immutable-registry validation. Fresh login resolves Codex 0.146.1 and Claude 2.1.223, but deployment is not considered successful. No blind retry; focused declarative lifecycle diagnosis/fix is in progress.

title: Subagent model selection is explicit and Sol cannot appear by omission
description: Codex spawned Sol subagents while Li believed exploration and implementation were using Luna and Terra. Session d04b76d9 records the prior default-model discussion. Current evidence shows role/default intent split across CriomOS-home and skills generation, while actual Codex runtime precedence was not witnessed. During the 2026-08-06 incident, full-history forks inherited the parent model and consumed unwanted Sol quota. A durable source change now emits Terra/xhigh in the non-orchestrator profile, but activation was cancelled under severe I/O pressure and the live profile still lacks model keys.
design: Define and wire explicit model selection at every spawn surface. Exploration is Luna; bounded implementation/default is Terra; Sol is never selected by omission or inheritance. Preserve explicit per-task overrides where the psyche directs them. Verification must capture effective runtime config and the actual model request, not only generated TOML or role files. Deploy only when the workstation is healthy enough, and verify ordinary orchestration and non-orchestrator paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Generated and live orchestrator, non-orchestrator, default, explorer, and worker paths have explicit intended models. 2. An omitted-model spawn is witnessed at runtime selecting Terra, never Sol. 3. An explorer spawn is witnessed selecting Luna. 4. Full-history/inheritance behavior cannot silently choose Sol. 5. Model identity and cost tier are visible in spawn/audit evidence. 6. Fix is committed, deployed, survives a fresh session, and session d04b76d9 concerns are closed with proof.

title: User environment remains coherent across deployments and agent work
description: Li's user environment repeatedly regresses after apparently successful fixes. Recurrent symptoms include Codex version rollback through competing Nix profile exposure, requested changes that are not activated or later shadowed, subagent model defaults claimed as Terra/Luna while omission selects Sol and exhausts paid quota, workstation slowdown from unconstrained agent activity, and accumulated Rust/Node/Nix build waste. The system spans Lojix, CriomOS, CriomOS-home, NixOS/Home Manager generations and activation, shell/session environment construction, Codex orchestration configuration, and long-lived agent/session practices. Session d04b76d9 contains primary context for the model-default failure. Existing resource-exhaustion incident primary-hh1 is related. This record owns the cross-session reliability program and first-pass audit; concrete findings become evidence-backed children.
design: Begin with read-only engine analysis and disk measurement. Trace real state owners and end-to-end activation/version/model-selection flows; label surfaces wired, stubbed, contract-only, conceptual, or stale. Preserve observations, inference, and unknowns separately. Fix source-of-truth and activation gaps rather than adding overlays. Use Luna explorers for broad cheap archaeology and Terra implementers for bounded changes; never use Sol subagents. Any cleanup must identify origin, regeneration contract, and recoverable size before deletion, then measure before/after. Develop a named long-lived workstation-integrity patrol only after its personality, memory, authority, cadence, and non-destructive boundaries are explicitly designed with the psyche.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Codex and other declared user tools cannot silently roll back or be shadowed by stale profile sources across login, Home Manager activation, Lojix deployment, or NixOS switch; witnessed regression checks cover the actual environment. 2. Every subagent spawn path has explicit auditable model policy: Luna exploration, Terra implementation/default, never Sol by omission, with a quota-visible witness. 3. Lojix/CriomOS/CriomOS-home ownership and activation flow is documented against real behavior, with stale and conceptual paths named. 4. Resource pressure and disk waste are inventoried; authorized regenerable data is reclaimed with before/after evidence and important state preserved. 5. A recurring named integrity patrol has approved vision, durable memory, bounded authority, and checkable reports. 6. Incident and deployment evidence survives sessions in child beads and reports.
notes: 2026-08-06 first-pass evidence. Immediate Codex rollback mechanism: generated session environment exported both the legacy home Nix profile and the XDG state profile; they contained conflicting Codex 0.146.0 vs 0.142.5 and Claude 2.1.220 vs 2.1.198. CriomOS main commit 0a7b20d1 removes the XDG state profile from PATH, NIX_PROFILES, and XDG lookup while preserving it on disk; source is pushed but system activation remains gated because it can disrupt the graphical session. Broader recurring pattern from read-only Luna audit: CriomOS embeds Home Manager while standalone Home Manager separately activates a user profile. Manual or standalone activation can change files and services, then reboot or system activation can reassert an older embedded generation. Historical report 0037 witnessed a live activation freeze and later reversion. Lojix also lacks reliable witnesses at several boundaries: accepted deployment may not mean activated; phase query may remain Building after terminal rejection; provenance and reboot convergence are incomplete. Session d04b76d9 shows Codex role-default intent existed in CriomOS-home but skills-generation wiring and actual runtime model precedence were not proven. Priority is one authoritative user-environment owner plus end-to-end deployment, activation, reboot, runtime-resolution, and model-request witnesses.

title: Protos engine rebuilt on 2026-08-04 syntax and encoded-type rulings

title: Delegated tool activity cannot exhaust the host or terminate its harness
description: Observed incident on 2026-08-02 (Europe/Madrid): a delegated worker began `nix develop -c tree-sitter test` at 16:05:12. PID 9995 reached 23,638,216 kB anonymous RSS and 67,122,824 kB total virtual memory. All 41,641,976 kB of swap was exhausted. The global OOM killer terminated the process at 16:08:30. At 16:10, after its stop timeout, systemd sent SIGKILL to the enclosing Ghostty shell; the agent harness died. Scope accounting recorded peaks of 23.1G RAM and 31.2G swap. The workstation was effectively frozen for minutes, ongoing agent state was lost with the harness, and work had to be reconstructed. The other concurrent worker used bounded commands and is not implicated. The exact trigger inside tree-sitter remains unknown. Goal: delegated tool activity must not be able to freeze the workstation or terminate the harness through host-wide resource exhaustion, and equivalent incidents must fail in a contained and observable way.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Representative resource-exhaustion behavior from delegated tool activity cannot make the workstation unresponsive, cause host-wide memory or swap exhaustion, or terminate the enclosing harness. 2. An equivalent excessive workload fails within its own scope while the workstation, enclosing shell, harness, and unrelated concurrent agent activity remain responsive. 3. The failure is observable with sufficient evidence to attribute its cause, resource impact, and affected scope. 4. The exact trigger inside the tree-sitter incident is identified with evidence, or the investigation records a defensible causal boundary and the remaining unknown explicitly. 5. The completed work includes checkable regression evidence for both containment of excessive activity and successful ordinary delegated activity.

title: testing skill — carry the witness doctrine forward with a travesty-guardrail line
description:
Problem: Agents across every repo keep writing prose-assertion tests — tests that assert document text content, whose failure is repaired by editing text to match the test rather than by fixing behavior. The testing skill is the authoring-time choke point; it must name this species and forbid it.

Authority: psyche ruling 2026-08-10 in psyche/Vision/testTravesties.md. See also primary-c2v (skills repo cleanup bead) for the live specimen.

Repo: LiGoldragon/skills (https://github.com/LiGoldragon/skills). Clone if absent: ghq get https://github.com/LiGoldragon/skills. The testing skill lives at .agents/skills/testing.md in that repo. Workspace copies (.claude/skills/, .pi/, etc.) are generated artifacts — never edit them directly; edit the source and redeploy.
design:
Substance to add (seed from corpus passages in primary/reports/PreResetCorpus-2026-06-07/skills/testing.md lines 113-125 and primary/reports/PreResetCorpus-2026-06-07/skills/architectural-truth-tests.md lines 43-45):

A test witnesses production behavior through a real boundary. A test that asserts the prose content of a document — or whose failure is repaired by editing text to match the test rather than by fixing behavior — is not a test. It is a travesty. Do not write it. Delete it or reroute it through the component's production API.

Key seed quote: 'If a test builds a miniature copy of the logic inside the test and then proves that copy works, it is not a witness. It is a self-contained story.'

HARD GATE — this is not negotiable: the exact skill wording must be shown to and approved by the psyche BEFORE any edit to the skill file. The worker's job is:
  1. Read the existing testing.md in LiGoldragon/skills.
  2. Read the corpus passages cited above for seed wording.
  3. Draft the new prose that will be inserted or appended.
  4. Route the draft to the psyche for approval via the psyche-interraction skill.
  5. Apply the approved wording only — no paraphrase, no improvement, no editorial discretion.

title: VSCodium lifecycle resists activation-launch races and hostile path collisions
description: The Bird incident fix is intentionally narrow and does not close every lifecycle concurrency boundary. Broader hardening remains: an exclusive-to-shared activation-release launch race; stale-root backup/restore time-of-check-to-time-of-use and no-clobber guarantees; and a comprehensive collision, tamper, and notifier-failure matrix. These findings are discovered follow-up work and do not block deploying the reviewed incident repair in primary-akw.
design: Specify the lifecycle state transition and lock ownership across activation handoff and launch before changing code. Eliminate the EX-to-SH release gap or make every replacement in that gap provably fail closed. Use direct atomic/no-clobber filesystem primitives for desired links and stale-root backup/restore, never precheck-then-overwrite sequences. Extend the sandboxed lifecycle/launcher fixtures to exercise adversarial path replacement and notification failure while preserving unrelated registry data. Keep the hardening declarative in CriomOS-home and expose its durable proof as Nix checks.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The activation-to-launch EX-to-SH transition has no unowned race window, or a deterministic test proves any contender causes a closed failure without launching VSCodium. 2. Stale-root backup and restore cannot clobber a path installed after validation; both collision directions have deterministic witnesses. 3. The matrix covers desired-link/root collisions; file, directory, and symlink tamper; backup and restore collisions; missing notifier; notifier failure; stderr visibility; and no underlying VSCodium execution on failure. 4. Unrelated extension-registry rows remain byte-for-byte semantically preserved. 5. Every durable witness is exposed through a CriomOS-home Nix check, and pushed source evidence records the exact test results. This bead does not gate the incident-scoped primary-akw deployment.

title: Stream MVP: StreamInitiation/StreamTermination types and Stream<Event> output
description: Design and implement the minimal Stream MVP, superseding the blocked primary-vq6.6 (old chain-binding/family-template stream design). StreamInitiation and StreamTermination are per-transformer types in nomos-types; Stream<Event> is the output object. The initiation payload shape and termination shape are agent-designed for now (provisional, for later psyche review per 2026-08-04 ruling). Psyche leanings from llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md: no stream section needed; initiating a stream requires a query and its establishment gives a response; StreamInitiation opens the door for StreamTermination naming; close arrives as its own input type, not a method on the Stream object.
design: Provisional xqb.3 schema: StreamInitiation carries only the typed query; StreamTermination carries the established typed StreamIdentity<Event>; success is Stream<Event> itself. protos owns pure StreamIdentity<Event>/Stream<Event> and signature-only StreamOpen/StreamEvent contracts. nomos-types owns only strict transformer schema. Core Ethos owns authored initiation and implies the separate generated termination input. Core Nomos directly lowers to an explicit archiveable Core Logos lifecycle object with no stream deferral surface. Rust Logos emits the contract; the generated component/witness owns registry, monotonic identity allocation, active queue, and closure behavior. No third universal close trait, no generic transformer envelope, no receipt/grant/token bridge, no Spirit work or persistence/restart.
acceptance_criteria: Authored strict StreamInitiation decodes and round-trips without the obsolete subscription wrapper. Nomos produces archive-roundtrippable explicit lifecycle Logos; deferred_stream_initiations, deferred_stream_terminations, Transformer::defer, and their public tests are removed rather than left empty. Emitted Rust returns Stream<Event> directly and compiles/runs in a named language-engine-witness Nix test that rejects one typed bad initiation query, establishes a typed identity, delivers one real typed event, terminates that same identity via a separate StreamTermination, and proves typed UnknownStream and AlreadyClosed termination refusals. The provisional fields and state ownership are documented in the owning code/design surface. protos-engine pins only published producers and verifies the owner proof. Spirit/signal-spirit remain untouched.
notes:
2026-08-04 implementation started in lane Xqb3StreamLifecycle20260804. Acceptance strengthened from the former compile-only wording to the confirmed zero-deferred vertical lifecycle proof.
2026-08-04 acceptance verified line by line. 1) Strict authored StreamInitiation decodes and round-trips without subscription wrapper: core-ethos 904dfce385ad9c7bfe0fa894267dd8815df100f4. 2) Core Nomos lowers archiveable lifecycle Logos directly; deferred stream APIs and tests removed: core-nomos 2e855607ebf4bc7f40b9328f8fbc78c59ed7926b. 3) Protos owns typed StreamIdentity/Stream/Event contracts: protos 95aeb1470c549a404518faf1ab0280a36583a2b3; transformer schema is in nomos-types a7b831e0540a8ad263cd07ed44ec4c95c56771fb; Core Logos resolution is a960aacff8ed13dc14b0ae0094208189d6609434. 4) Emitted Rust returns Stream<Event> and names InvalidQuery, UnknownStream, AlreadyClosed: rust-logos 306098361221b0f19b82156ab697134520fce8bc. 5) Named witness compiles actual emitted contract and proves typed bad initiation, monotonic identity, one event, separate termination, AlreadyClosed and UnknownStream: language-engine-witness 37dffb34e355e526b311f6a4d3f8c4764caca668. 6) Sink pins only published producers and validates direct ownership: protos-engine merge 2191239f91e04b479de1157721ea2f399e42744c. 7) This lane had no Spirit, signal-spirit, or meta-signal-spirit claims; signal-spirit and meta-signal-spirit are clean. The dirty spirit checkout is independently protected by DotosOrphanRecovery and was neither written nor cleaned by this slice. Validation: producer Nix/Rust checks, merged nix flake check --option eval-cache false --option substituters quote quote -L, and nix run .#check-all all passed. All eight touched producer/sink worktrees are clean and synchronized with git/origin main; generated witness result symlinks removed.
Correction to the validation transcription above: the exact merged flake command was nix flake check --option eval-cache false --option substituters '' -L.

title: nomos-types shared repository created with per-transformer data types
description: Create the nomos-types shared repository holding pure per-transformer data types (StreamInitiation, StreamTermination, etc.) consumed by both core-ethos and core-nomos. Transformer trait and implementations remain in Nomos. Hand-written mirror for now; end state is types authored once in Ethos and shared. Related: primary-qdn (Ethos/Nomos transformer schema mirroring). Ruling: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md "nomos-types shared crate; transformer implementations stay in Nomos".
design: Repository lifecycle skill governs repo creation. Pure data types only — no trait definitions, no impl blocks. Each transformer gets its own strict type carrying its full input schema. The Ethos-side mirror of these types is hand-written for now. Mirroring law: each daemon holds types that store the objects belonging to the next daemon down the chain (Ethos/Nomos and Nomos/Logos). Sema is the shared database engine, not a chain daemon.
acceptance_criteria: nomos-types repository exists at /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/nomos-types with per-transformer data types; both core-ethos and core-nomos depend on it; types compile; the transformer trait lives in Nomos, not in nomos-types.
notes:
Implemented and published: public nomos-types main 183f76c74270fa54cc0d0ad84e860c542240e957 exposes data-only StreamInitiation and StreamTermination (rkyv archive/restore test; no traits or impls; Cargo/Nix checks green). Core Nomos d832b9e1e308706b9e3c0205fc8a637d9de8ea00 pins that exact Ethos revision, owns Transformer impls for both shared carriers, and test-proves identity-preserving deferred_stream_terminations. No Stream lifecycle/runtime behavior was introduced.

title: Syntax revision lands in dotos and core-ethos codecs
description: Implement the 2026-08-04 syntax rulings in the dotos parser/writer and core-ethos codec. New surface: “ ” strings (balanced nesting + \\“ \\” \\\\ escapes, minimal-common-indent blocks) replacing ( ) text and (| |)/[| |] pipe-text which are dropped; bare Rust-style < > generics (exclusive to generics); transformer applications Name.Transformer.(…) standalone and Name.(…) sectioned; bare | retired from the grammar. Unchanged: .{ struct, .[ enum, .Symbol newtype. Co-designed with strict encoded types (primary-0l8): text form and encoded type are one design act (design-by-parsing). Repos: /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/dotos, /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/core-ethos. Rulings: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md, design/ProtosEngine/universalNamePrefixTransformerPipe-2026-08-03.md.
design: Design-by-parsing: every syntax change is co-designed with its encoded type (primary-0l8). The dot-prefix stays confirmed (Name.{). The application dot never separates from its delimiter. String escapes: balanced “” pairs nest without escapes; unbalanced literal “ or ” is \\“ or \\”; literal backslash is \\\\. Guillemets «» are approved delimiters with no assigned slot (disfavored for wire use by tokenizer-variance evidence). Non-string uses of ( ) such as Map-headed application are not addressed. Generics: Vector<Sortable>, Result<Vector<Sortable> Error>. No complex struct/enum form.
acceptance_criteria: Dotos parser accepts the new string/generics/transformer syntax and rejects the dropped forms; core-ethos codec round-trips all new forms; existing golden fixtures updated; all Nix gates green.
notes:
Declaration grammar closed by 2026-08-04 rulings (design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md): generic pickup by use — a <Trait> mention in a field/variant/method position IS the parameter declaration, no parameter head; bare same-trait mentions co-refer (one parameter, all mentions lock to the same type at instantiation); distinct parameters sharing a trait use the named form <Left.Sortable> <Right.Sortable>. Qualities ontology confirmed: Quality.[Shape Trait] — Shape = engine constructors (Vector/Option/Map; unbounded, not generics, never authored), Trait = contractual quality, the only authored parameterization, always bounded, no universal trait. One angle syntax for both; resolution classifies by declaration site; bare pickup slots accept Trait only. Rust emission: type parameter carries the trait proper name (struct Sorted<Ordered: Ord>), via the correctNaming table (primary-xqb.7).
Family-wide scope (psyche, 2026-08-04): the syntax revision applies to ALL protos-family surfaces, dotos included. Dotos operative impact: “ ” replaces ( ) multi-word text and the dropped pipe-text (| |)/[| |] — the string carrier is the one dotos-visible change; .( ) transformer marking reads uniformly (Map.(…) consistent). {} structs, [] vectors, dotted variant paths, ;; comments, bare atoms unchanged; <> qualities are type-side only since position supplies the type in data. The dotos codec migration is in scope of this bead, not a separate concern.
Direct contract boundary after strict audit: Dotos main 2db2eb91e8ae8f5a979af5b85762abceb823445d proves standalone Name.Transformer.(...) and sectioned Name.(...) parser shapes. Core-Ethos main 841674c82b61fcaabd67dc1d7d2636c5bdbec31a proves strict WholeEthosMethod sectioned name.(...) round-trip/refusal and nested Result<Vector<Ordered> Error>. Standalone Name.Transformer.(...) cannot round-trip through a strict existing Core-Ethos type: its only current mapping is forbidden/deferred WholeEthosOperatorApplication { operator, name, fields: Vec<WholeEthosTypeReference> }. xqb.1 now explicitly depends on xqb.2 (nomos-types/per-transformer data types); that edge was checked for cycles before addition. Keep xqb.1 open until xqb.2 supplies the strict transformer schema.
Post-xqb.2 strict Core witness: language-engine-witness now pins Core Ethos 3fd3faa3210a2a36f0c803c9319a6776068c1c72, Core Nomos d832b9e1e308706b9e3c0205fc8a637d9de8ea00, Core Logos f02ce18c93f85ce44e6e2e291a2bd514346eccbe, Rust Logos 5e0a5690e674c72a7c69af74d077e6a386aea722, and structural-codec d3b7d2bacf8bb72db63d9a25f20d489bcfc8219c. Its strict isolated authored fixture decodes Observer.Stream.(WireEnvelope WireProduct WireChoice), defers exact roles through Nomos Transformer, lowers declarations to Logos, emits Rust, and compiles/runs the archive witness; cargo test --test nexus and nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.test pass. It preserves old batch runtime fixtures on their old aliases rather than changing runtime behavior. xqb.1 remains open: Core Nomos explicitly refuses n-ary ruled applications with UnsupportedTypeApplicationArity while Core Logos remains unary, so the required nested n-ary full witness cannot close until the Core Logos/Rust Logos capability is published.
N-ary blocker resolved. Published Core Logos 39c9cbbd8bcdfb7a6eadf26cab044c5ba4607cb9: non-empty ordered WholeLogosTypeApplication arguments, archive validation/versioned identity, nested archive witness. Published Rust Logos 90367f7d8ebf0ceb757b06d3ada99fefc86e0c16: every application argument validates, structural reify/reflect round-trips, and Rust emission renders ordered n-ary forms. Published Core Nomos 74f86d71e9dea42c6f23411ae0a5120f8d3b3e6c: lowers every n-ary argument and fingerprints count plus ordered argument shapes. Language witness 89c49ee98ba5dd6c068326d3e75e9475be05d97f authors strict WireResult.Result<Vector<Ordered> Error>, verifies emitted pub struct WireResult(Result<Vec<Ord>, Error>);, and archive/restores it in a scratch run alongside WireChoice. nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.test -L passes provisioned full tests; build/doc/fmt/clippy/spirit-domain/offline checks pass (only an ignored Nix eval-cache SQLite-busy notice). Old batch aliases remain untouched, so no runtime/xqb.3 change is included.
Quality-pickup correction supersedes the prior incorrect n-ary witness interpretation. Core Ethos 038dbeb6ba09eaa27341be9d917b5c1cb08abf72 retains bare Ordered as a picked-up parameter with explicit {name: Ordered, quality: Ordered}; Core Logos c40045842c2322fc1e66d30b9f4ef2e1468428e5 retains the proper parameter name plus trait-bound carrier; Core Nomos ce87da1d14b644888cf709b119995e6aab47741b lowers both losslessly; Rust Logos 6c6cfab3d558ad7c1effb91ecb83521a9d69d518 uses contextual correctNaming translation, retaining Ordered at parameter/type-use sites and mapping it to Ord only at the trait-bound site. language-engine-witness 91d5ef12a9eb58afd4ce2e06b5c21486c5200169 pins exactly those revisions and proves authored WireResult.Result<Vector<Ordered> Error> emits pub struct WireResult<Ordered: Ord>(Result<Vec<Ordered>, Error>); then instantiates concrete archiveable Ordered and archive/restores the generic result plus WireChoice. All focused/full Cargo, docs, clippy, and Nix producer gates pass; the provisioned language witness Nix test plus build/doc/fmt/clippy/spirit/offline checks pass (only ignored Nix eval-cache SQLite-busy notices). xqb.3 runtime remains untouched.
Final acceptance audit 2026-08-04: SATISFIED and independently rerun. DOTOS main@origin 2db2eb91e8ae8f5a979af5b85762abceb823445d is clean. tests/next_gen_grammar.rs proves curly strings, nested bare-angle Result<Vector<Ordered> Error>, standalone Name.Transformer.(...), sectioned Name.(...), and rejection of legacy parenthesized and pipe strings plus dot-prefixed angle syntax; nix flake check -L passed. Core Ethos main@origin 038dbeb6ba09eaa27341be9d917b5c1cb08abf72 is clean. tests/spirit_fixtures.rs round-trips curly import strings, picked-up nested generic references, Name.(...) methods, and Observer.Stream.(...); it rejects retired dotted/pipe/brace alternatives. The three reviewed golden fixtures interface.ethos, nexus.ethos, and sema.ethos decode, canonical-emit, re-decode identically, and archive/restore; core-ethos nix flake check -L passed. The full compiled/running process witness is language-engine-witness main@origin 91d5ef12a9eb58afd4ce2e06b5c21486c5200169, clean: its strict source emits pub struct WireResult<Ordered: Ord>(Result<Vec<Ordered>, Error>); and its Nix test builds/runs concrete generic archive/restore alongside WireChoice. Reran nix flake check -L and nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.test -L successfully. Supporting full Nix checks passed for core-logos c40045842c2322fc1e66d30b9f4ef2e1468428e5, core-nomos ce87da1d14b644888cf709b119995e6aab47741b, rust-logos 6c6cfab3d558ad7c1effb91ecb83521a9d69d518, nomos-types 183f76c74270fa54cc0d0ad84e860c542240e957, raw-discovery 2d4e2e00f2821c4e2893fa96028cef0ac76e9644, and structural-codec 16b28bf6028af6891db32a23300c401accbca5ec. All listed repos have clean working copies and local main equals main@origin.
close_reason: Final audit verified each original clause with rerun Nix gates, updated goldens, exact clean main@origin revisions, and the compiled/running strict language witness; detailed durable evidence is in the final audit note.

description: Gate open: traitVocabularyRulings-2026-08-07 and textualFormMetadataStore-2026-08-07 have landed, unblocking implementation. title: Projection profiles: token-lean canonical and pretty-printed human projections
description: Implement the two projection profiles the psyche confirmed as a standing given: a token-lean canonical single-line projection for agent consumption, and a pretty-printed projection for human editing. Both are legal because round-trip correctness is encoded-value equivalence (design/ProtosEngine/encodedMeaningRoundTrip-2026-08-02.md). Measured: block layout costs +33% to +102% over single-line records (newline+indent never merges; closing delimiter fuses with newline for free). Ruling: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md "projection profiles".
design: Engine emits both projections from the same encoded value. The canonical single-line projection minimizes token count for agent/LLM consumption. The pretty-printed projection uses indentation and newlines for human readability. No semantic difference between the two — encoded-value equivalence is the round-trip invariant.
acceptance_criteria: The engine can emit both projections for any valid encoded value; canonical projection is demonstrably single-line and token-lean; pretty-printed projection is human-readable; both round-trip to the same encoded value.

title: Traits-ontology standing directive: soft requirement with per-repo migration files
description: Record the traits-ontology standing directive so implementers discover it. Traits are the code ontology; the target is 100% of impls living under a trait. This is a SOFT requirement on hand-written Rust: encouraged, not blocking. Where a trait is not obvious, implementers note the case in a trait-migration file in that repo for later psyche review. Not a mass-refactor pass. Ruling: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md "traits are a soft requirement with per-repo trait-migration files".
design: Create or verify trait-migration.md (or equivalent) exists in each protos-train repository. The file convention: implementers add entries when they write an impl that has no obvious trait home. The psyche reviews these files later with a Claude agent. No existing code is forcibly refactored by this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The directive is recorded in a discoverable location (design log or per-repo); at least the core protos-train repositories have trait-migration files; no mass refactoring performed.

title: Ethos carries Nomos transformer input schemas (daemon-chain type mirroring)
description: Ruled 2026-08-04: transformer applications are Name.Transformer.(…) and Ethos must know the input schema of each Nomos transformer to type the payloads — a type-mirroring layer parallel to the existing Logos/Nomos mirroring. Implied general law: each daemon holds types that store the objects belonging to the next daemon down the chain. Parsing stays table-free (.( marks transformer applications structurally); the schemas are for typing, not parsing. Context: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md. Relevant repos: core-ethos, core-nomos, nomos-engine at /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/.
acceptance_criteria: Ethos can type-check a transformer application payload against the Nomos transformer input schema, with the mirroring mechanism designed and recorded; parser remains free of any Nomos table.
notes:
Rulings 2026-08-04: no generic transformer-application node — one strict type per transformer (StreamInitiation, StreamTermination, …) carrying the transformer's FULL input schema. Mirror is hand-written for now; end state: types authored once in Ethos, that Ethos source shared between Nomos and Ethos (repetition eliminated). Sema is the shared database engine, not a chain daemon; mirroring binds Ethos/Nomos and Nomos/Logos.
Related to primary-xqb.2 (nomos-types shared repository) in the 2026-08-04 deep redesign. The nomos-types repo is the first concrete step toward the type-mirroring this bead describes. Hand-written mirror for now; end state is types authored once in Ethos.

title: “ ” and « » are easy to type in the editing environment
description: Ruled 2026-08-04: “ ” (U+201C/U+201D) replaces ( ) and (| |) as the Dotos string carrier, with common-indentation semantics; « » (U+00AB/U+00BB) is approved but slotless. The psyche currently copy-pastes these characters — there is no input method. Needed: an easy, declarative way to type both pairs (compose key, layout, or editor binding). The OS is declarative: system source /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/CriomOS, user environment /git/github.com/LiGoldragon/CriomOS-home. Ruling context: design/ProtosEngine/llmTokenOptimizationRulings-2026-08-04.md. The psyche will drive this with a dedicated agent; do not fold it into protos engine work.
acceptance_criteria: The psyche can type “ ” and « » directly in his normal editor/terminal without copy-paste, via a declaratively configured input method.

title: Nomos train Rust sources contain no forbidden tuples
description: The baseline pickup surface is reports/RustTupleViolationsRegister-2026-07-30.md: 27 multi-field tuple structs plus its ad-hoc tuple returns and tuple-typed fields and collections. Reconciliation on 2026-08-02 also found cases absent or misclassified in that register: name-table src/archive.rs receipts is inside versioned rkyv ArchiveState; explicit source tuple types at structural-codec src/table.rs:409 and src/evaluator.rs:546, nomos-engine src/store.rs:637, and sema-translator src/wire.rs:31; generated core-nomos public decode contracts emit Result tuple types; the compiled closure retains legacy name-table revision 196610e2907687dcb8dbd0d2dfaafe4aefd9fa27 with tuple APIs at src/table.rs:117 and :446; structural-codec tests/disjointness.rs is named by the register but is not a registered Cargo test target. Clean the current Nomos-train closure in producer-first vertical slices without conflating lawful single-field newtypes with forbidden tuples.
design: Work one repository at a time in dependency order, publishing each producer before immutable downstream repins. Before converting each archived tuple carrier, forged archive-compatible carrier, or tuple collection nested in a versioned archive, first land an empirical archive witness for that exact shape. The witness must preserve field types and declaration order and prove byte equality, archived size and alignment equality, cross-access, cross-restoration, and byte-exact reserialization using distinct nonempty values. A failed or non-reproducible witness defers that conversion; never conceal incompatibility with an archive version or identity bump. Convert non-archived cases to small named-field carriers and update every constructor, accessor, helper, and consumer. Treat generated public decode tuples, generated-output ownership, legacy name-table alias removal, inactive test-target coverage, and any unclear archive case as separately reviewed gates rather than mechanical sweep work.
acceptance_criteria: Rescan all landed train revisions and their active source and test targets against reports/RustTupleViolationsRegister-2026-07-30.md plus every newly discovered case, and record the reconciled disposition. Every converted archived shape has its pre-conversion compatibility witness retained and passing. Every landed repository passes focused tests and its full nix flake check -L gate; downstream manifests and locks pin the exact published producer revisions. No forbidden tuple remains in the current closure except cases explicitly deferred with path, reason, evidence, and follow-up tracking. Unclear archive compatibility, generated public contracts or generated-output ownership, the legacy name-table alias revision, and inactive or missing test coverage must be explicitly deferred rather than silently omitted.

description:

title: Ethos and Dotos express general data anatomy outside component roles
description: The current stage intentionally standardizes Interface, Nexus, and Sema for bootstrap components. Later, Dotos data used by an agent harness, Mentci view model, compiler interchange, scientific corpus, or configuration may need anatomy that is not intrinsically a wire interface, daemon machinery, or persisted Sema table. primary-pjm already explored a minimal types-only root as a file-kinds-law witness, so this outcome must reconcile that evidence rather than duplicate its implementation or reopen the current three schemas.
design: At the later Ethos and Dotos language-growth stage, decide whether neutral data anatomy is a dedicated typed file kind, an ordinary module root, or another more elegant composition of existing concepts. Preserve header, imports, body, context-driven parsing, encoded identity, and non-repetition. Distinguish logical data anatomy from Sema physical persistence and from Interface transport roles. Use real harness, GUI, and compiler-data examples; do not presume that a new file kind is the answer.
acceptance_criteria: A psyche-reviewed or explicitly delegated decision gives general Dotos data a precise schema home and strict encoded root, or demonstrates compositionally why no additional home is needed. Dotos instances for an LLM harness response, a GUI view model, and compiler interchange data round-trip from discoverable Ethos anatomy without pretending to be database tables or signal messages. Ownership and reuse relative to Interface, Nexus, Sema, and modules are explicit. primary-pjm is then closed, superseded, or related with a durable explanation rather than duplicated.

title: Unsafe and hardware interaction have an explicit target-independent Logos boundary
description: The eventual LLVM and operating-system replacements require Logos to describe operations that ordinary safe code cannot: concrete layout and address spaces, raw memory access, volatile and atomic operations, device registers, interrupts, calling conventions, intrinsics, foreign boundaries, and target capabilities. No current bead defines that boundary, and inheriting Rust unsafe blocks or LLVM IR as the ontology would violate the self-hosting direction.
design: Define a narrow, explicit semantic boundary between ordinary typed behavior and operations whose correctness depends on declared machine or foreign contracts. Keep targets and capabilities as typed data rather than parser or backend constants. Make authority, preconditions, and unverifiable obligations inspectable. Use concrete hardware examples to falsify the design while avoiding one architecture or operating system as the universal model.
acceptance_criteria: A psyche-reviewed or explicitly delegated schema decision defines target descriptions, capability requirements, safety obligations, and the strict Logos forms needed for raw memory, volatile access, atomics, interrupts, foreign calls, and target-specific intrinsics. Witnesses represent an MMIO device operation, an atomic synchronization primitive, an interrupt entry, and a foreign calling boundary; ordinary code cannot perform them without the declared boundary. At least two target descriptions demonstrate that the schema is not Rust-, LLVM-, ABI-, architecture-, or current-OS-specific.

title: Temporal protocols are typed across complete interaction lifecycles
description: The bootstrap Interface categories and Stream MVP describe the present component boundary, but they do not yet claim to be the universal semantics of sessions and distributed interaction. Later runtime growth must represent allowed message order, correlation, state transitions, deadlines, cancellation, backpressure, retry and idempotency, partial failure, and protocol completion without adding ad hoc sections to the current file kinds.
design: Treat a protocol as compositional typed behavior whose legal transitions and invariants are explicit in Logos and whose data is rendered in Dotos. Determine how protocol state relates to traits, effects, resources, and Interface declarations. Validate the ontology against request and response, a bidirectional backpressured stream, and a replicated or retrying interaction. Do not require this work for the existing Spirit stream witness.
acceptance_criteria: A psyche-reviewed or explicitly delegated schema decision defines protocol roles, states, transitions, correlation, completion, and failure semantics. Strict witnesses accept the valid lifecycle and reject an invalid transition for request and response, bidirectional stream with backpressure and cancellation, and a retrying or replicated interaction with an idempotency invariant. The relationship to bootstrap Interface and Stream declarations is explicit, and no change is required of primary-vq6.8.

title: Effects, resources, and concurrency compose as typed Logos semantics
description: Complete runtime behavior needs more than control flow. Protos has not yet ruled how observable effects, mutable state, acquisition and release, ownership or borrowing, failure and cancellation, asynchronous tasks, synchronization, and nondeterminism appear in Logos. Copying Rust async, Rust borrowing, POSIX threads, or one operating-system handle model would make a bootstrap substrate permanent. This question deliberately belongs to the later Logos slice.
design: Compare candidate ontologies against beauty, strictness, local reasoning, and composability, then choose one coherent typed model rather than independent special cases. Separate timeless values from resources and effects; make cleanup, cancellation, and concurrency relationships visible in encoded form. Express target/runtime support through traits or capabilities where that is the elegant logic. Coordinate with the core executable schema and temporal-protocol child.
acceptance_criteria: A psyche-reviewed or explicitly delegated decision defines the strict Logos representations and composition laws for effects, resource lifecycle, and concurrency. Witnesses cover deterministic acquisition and release of a resource, an effect-constrained computation, two coordinated tasks, cancellation, failure propagation, and race or synchronization behavior. Invalid ownership or lifecycle composition is rejected structurally or by typing. The schema does not encode Rust lifetimes, Rust futures, POSIX threads, or current-OS handles as universal concepts.

title: Logos behavior schema represents executable programs completely
description: WholeLogos now carries declaration vocabulary such as structs, traits, and trait implementations, but the staged train does not yet give executable bodies a complete strict schema. Before Protos can replace compiler, GUI, service, and operating-system implementations, Logos must explicitly represent what programs do without treating a Rust syntax tree as truth. This is future Logos work, not a missing requirement of the current Spirit bootstrap.
design: Derive the smallest elegant executable algebra from program semantics: bindings and values, calls, selection and pattern handling, repetition or recursion, returns and refusals, composition under traits, and the relationship between behavior bodies and declarations. Keep effects, resource discipline, concurrency, protocols, and hardware boundaries explicit through sibling outcomes rather than smuggling them into generic expression nodes. Nomos transforms encoded Ethos into these strict Logos objects; Rust or another backend is a projection.
acceptance_criteria: A psyche-reviewed or explicitly delegated schema decision names every executable object and its composition laws. Strict encoded Logos round-trips representative behavior for a recursive pure algorithm, a compiler-style tree transformation, and a stateful handler. Trait implementation bodies connect to the existing declaration vocabulary without generic untyped containers. A derived executable projection preserves observed results, and no required semantic field is Rust-, LLVM-, or current-OS-specific.

title: Logos carries complete executable behavior without a permanent substrate
description: Current staged Protos covers interface and type declarations while executable behavior remains handwritten Rust. The renewed 2026-08-06 psyche vision says this is intentional until the Logos slice and is not a defect or gate of primary-vq6.8. Logos is destined to be the complete explicit program representation, with Rust only a bootstrap textual projection. This epic owns the later behavior-schema questions. Authority: reports/deep-vision/protos-engine-renewed-vision-2026-08-06.md. Existing foundations: primary-vq6.2, primary-xqb, and primary-qdn.
design: Start only as a later Logos language-growth slice; do not reopen or delay the current Interface, Nexus, Sema, or Spirit stage. Design strict purpose-specific encoded behavior from semantic needs, then derive textual and executable projections. Do not encode Rust, LLVM, or current operating-system syntax as the semantic model. Child work separates the core executable algebra, effects and resources and concurrency, temporal protocols, and unsafe or hardware interaction so each concern can be judged explicitly and then composed.
acceptance_criteria: All child outcomes are closed with durable schema decisions and witnesses. The complete strict Logos representation round-trips and covers at least a pure algorithm, a stateful asynchronous interaction, a typed protocol lifecycle, and a hardware-bound primitive; at least one executable projection is derived from that representation; no schema assumes Rust, LLVM, or the current OS as permanent; and this epic was never used to delay or broaden primary-vq6.8.

title: signal-nomos d47 compatibility dev-dep keeps an old family subtree in the graph
description: signal-nomos's dev-dependency d47-core-nomos (package core-nomos, rev d47e1e4441b7, v0.26.0) exists solely for tests/compatibility_d47.rs::d47_core_readers_refuse_the_appended_recursive_and_insert_at_tags, which needs a live old reader to prove old readers refuse the appended Recursive and InsertAt tags. That single dev-dep drags an entire stale subtree into Cargo.lock: protos 1343d0c4 and c85cec61, core-logos 141abe23, core-ethos 47c866f1, rust-logos 96eda934, signal-sema-translator 51c02c4a, structural-codec 1485c1f8, raw-discovery 7290f65b, name-table 50cb4bb5, content-identity fdf2db1d. The normal (non-dev) graph is already single-copy at the family heads after primary-bxi; only the dev graph is doubled. Elsewhere in the family the compatibility idiom is frozen golden bytes (core-nomos: 'test: freeze d47 authored archive compatibility'), not an old-revision dev-dep. Retiring the dev-dep either loses the old-reader-refuses guarantee or requires reexpressing it against frozen bytes — a test redesign, not mechanical fallout, so primary-bxi deliberately left it in place.
acceptance_criteria: Psyche or design ruling on whether the old-reader-refuses guarantee is kept (reexpressed against frozen goldens) or retired; if retired, signal-nomos's dev graph is single-copy at the family heads too.
close_reason: Verified 2026-08-07: signal-nomos origin/main (commit 44188eb) has no d47 dev-dependency, test, or golden. Only a guard test asserting absence remains. Note: the guard test itself is flagged to the psyche as a possible refusal-proof violation under anything-old-must-die.

title: Tree-sitter grammar updates for dotos and ethos
description: Update the tree-sitter grammars for dotos (tree-sitter-dotos) and ethos to reflect the 2026-08-04 syntax rulings. Both grammars are stale and now further invalidated by: curly-quote strings replacing round-paren text and pipe-text; bare angle-bracket generics; .Transformer.(…) applications; bare pipe retirement. Low priority — the engine codecs are the source of truth; tree-sitter is for editor support.
design: Update grammar.js for tree-sitter-dotos and tree-sitter-ethos. Add rules for " " string literals with balanced nesting and escape sequences; < > generic parameters; .Transformer.(…) and Name.(…) applications. Remove rules for ( ) text, (| |) pipe-text, [| |], bare | transformer syntax. Regenerate and test.
acceptance_criteria: tree-sitter-dotos and tree-sitter-ethos parse valid new-syntax files correctly; highlights work in editors; old dropped syntax is no longer accepted by the grammar.
